seed: Objects of type `reflection` under action ACTION1 with touching neighbours [reflection,target] show mixed outcomes: h,pixels,w x1, gone x1. Find the condition in the before state that decides the outcome. Start from this kind of condition: a field of the object itself, such as its tags, pixels, visibility or layer. Verify it against every transition before you keep it.

synth.notes:
Axis wall moves with ACTION1/2 when selected; ACTION1-4 move the selected 3x3-cell piece by 3; ACTION5 cycles the selection axis -> pieces.
Each piece is mirrored across the axis as a gray reflection. The frame is drawn in layers wall1 < target2 < reflection3 < piece4, then objects are re-read as 4-connected components.
Hole centres: transparent over lower content; otherwise 0 for the selected object (reflections fill them with 4). Targets are rebuilt per 3x3 block; wall_h index is its (x,y) rank among walls and visible 0-holes.
Hypothesis answer: a reflection disappears when it touches another reflection and they merge into one component under re-extraction; no field of the object itself decides it.
Unconfirmed (no data): blocking at bounds or on piece overlap, ACTION5 wrapping back to the axis, vertical axes. Passes with hidden state disabled.
